subject: calculus
subtopics: the limit of a function at a point, and the informal epsilon-delta meaning
one-sided limits, and the condition under which the two-sided limit exists
the algebra of limits: sums, products, quotients and compositions, with their hypotheses
the standard limits at zero: sin x / x, (1 - cos x)/x^2, (e^x - 1)/x, (a^x - 1)/x, ln(1 + x)/x, (1 + x)^(1/x)
indeterminate forms 0/0 and infinity/infinity, and L'Hopital's rule with its three conditions
the forms 0 times infinity, infinity minus infinity, 0^0, infinity^0 and 1^infinity, and their conversions
limits at infinity, and the order of growth of logarithms, powers and exponentials
continuity at a point: the three conditions, and one-sided continuity at an endpoint
the types of discontinuity: removable, jump, infinite and oscillatory
continuity on an interval, and the algebra and composition of continuous functions
the Intermediate Value Theorem, its sign-change corollary and its use on a constructed function
differentiability at a point, one-sided derivatives, and differentiability implying continuity
the geometric causes of non-differentiability: corners, cusps and vertical tangents
piecewise functions: matching the value and the slope at a join
differentiation rules needed inside these questions: chain rule, product and quotient rules

chosen.title: 11 Oct - EM - Calculus Part 2, GATE Guidance live class (1 hr 4 min)
covers: rationalisation as the first technique for an indeterminate limit, worked on (3 - sqrt(5 + x))/(x - 4) at x = 4
the Maclaurin series of log(1 + x), log(1 - x), e^x, e^-x, sin x and cos x, used to expand a limit
L'Hopital's rule with the 0/0 and infinity/infinity conditions, and repeated differentiation
limits at infinity solved by dividing by the dominant exponential
continuity at a point as three conditions, with a hole and a jump drawn
the properties of continuous functions, including composition
differentiability by the difference quotient, and the geometric meaning of a sharp corner, worked on |x|
GATE CSE 2013 (continuity at a join) and GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 Q.2 (degree of a derivative) solved in class
chosen.why: The only GATE-oriented lecture on this topic whose content could be read this run, and it follows the order a beginner needs: limit techniques, then continuity, then differentiability, with the GATE questions solved at the end rather than at the start. It is a Hindi-medium class, and what was readable is the platform's published English chapter summary with timestamps, not a transcript, so the cards use its structure, its technique order and its worked question choices, and no card quotes a sentence of the lecturer. The class's own arithmetic was re-derived before use: (3 - sqrt(5 + x))/(x - 4) at x = 4 has limit -1/6, and (e^x - 1)/(x^2 + x) at 0 has limit 1, both recomputed in scripts/validate.py.

chosen.title: Calculus I, Chapter 2 (Limits) and section 2.9 (Continuity)
chosen.channel: Paul's Online Math Notes, Lamar University
covers: the limit at a point, one-sided limits and the limit properties
computing limits by factoring, rationalising and the squeeze theorem
infinite limits and limits at infinity
the definition of continuity and the note that both f(a) and the limit must exist
jump and removable discontinuities, named and explained on a graph
the Intermediate Value Theorem, with the warning that it verifies a value but never excludes one and does not say how many times
chosen.why: Chosen for correctness and for beginner accessibility, not for exam framing: it is the one readable English source this run that states every definition and hypothesis the cards depend on, including the two conditions inside the continuity definition that the 2013 question tests. Read in full. It carries no GATE material, so it supplies definitions only; every exam claim in the topic comes from a verified previous-year question.

chosen.title: NOC: Basic Calculus - 1, Prof. Arindama Singh, IIT Madras
covers: the week-by-week order: limits and one-sided limits in week 2, continuity and the intermediate value property in week 3, differentiation and the chain rule in week 4
confirmation that this topic is three weeks of a twelve-week course, which fixes the scope of this run
chosen.why: Recorded as structure only, and it is the reason the subtopic enumeration runs limit, then continuity, then differentiability rather than interleaving them. It is the closest NPTEL course to the syllabus line and its outline is readable, but no lecture transcript could be read, so no card quotes it and no claim rests on it.

notes: No video transcript was readable this run. YouTube answered LOGIN_REQUIRED ('Sign in to confirm you are not a bot') for every watch page, yt-dlp returned HTTP 403, and the consent cookie did not help, so the one GATE-oriented lecture in the chosen list is recorded from the platform's published English chapter summary with timestamps and is marked SUMMARY_ONLY. No card quotes a lecturer's sentence and no card claims a timestamp for a claim that is not in that summary.

The syllabus names the topic in five words, so the fifteen subtopics above are this run's enumeration from the standard treatment (Thomas, Stewart, NCERT chapter 5) and the eleven verified CSE questions, not a quotation from the syllabus.

The non-English material is one Hindi-medium GATE lecture, marked translated. What was readable is an English AI summary of it, so the translation sits two layers from the lecture - summary, then English - and the cards say so rather than implying a verbatim translation.

Maxima and minima, the mean value theorem and integration are the next three topics in the cycle. Questions that belong to them, such as GATE CSE 2021 Set 2 Q.25 (f'(x) <= 2 with f(-3) = 7) and GATE CSE 2023 Q.28 (local maxima of a cubic), were deliberately left for those runs and are not in this topic's PYQ set.
